subject: SLO measurement, dashboard access checklist & temporary exemption request
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightside.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightside.com
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLO measurement questions + request for interim access

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran our standard SLO questionnaire and a couple of items need clarification before we can finish the security review. Two things in particular: 1) How do you compute the availability SLO for multi-tenant hosted instances (window, sampling, and noisy-neighbor mitigation)? 2) Can Brightside get read-only access to the uptime/latency dashboards for a 30-day onboarding window (we'll disable after go-live)?

I'm attaching the questionnaire with line items highlighted. If you can point us to the exact metrics and the expected measurement windows (e.g., 1 minute vs 5 minutes, rolling 7d/30d), that will speed things up. Also include any temporary exemption process (if you cannot meet a metric during migration).

Best,
Anna Liu
Senior Procurement Lead
Brightside Health

Attachment: Brightside_SLO_Questionnaire.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightside.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement questions + request for interim access

Anna —

Thanks for sending this — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front, and we'll follow with a short packet and links: 1) Availability SLO (hosted): we compute by region/route as percent of successful request completions per minute, aggregated into rolling 30-day windows for contractual reporting. Shorter sampling (1-min / 5-min) is used for alerting and root-cause but contract breaches use the 30-day rolling window. 2) Read-only dashboard access: we can grant a time-limited Grafana link (RBAC) for a 30-day onboarding window. Security will need to approve the view.

Kimberly, Marcus — can you validate the wording below and confirm what telemetry we should surface to Brightside (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, request success by model version, synthetic-check pass rate)? Also: Sofia's team is running a migration next week; if there's any predicted SLO drift we may offer a documented temporary exemption period (up to 14 days) with mitigations — Kimberly, can you outline the approval path?

I'll attach the brief packet in a follow-up.

—Jordan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightside.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement questions + request for interim access

Anna/Jordan —

Adding the telemetry set we typically expose for procurement review: 1) Availability % (successful 2xx responses / total requests) — contractual: rolling 30-day; alerting: 5-min aggregates with 1-min sampling. 2) Error rate by code bucket (4xx/5xx) with per-route breakdown. 3) Latency percentiles: p50/p95/p99 measured at request completion; contractual p95 on the 30-day window. 4) Synthetic health checks (region-level, 1-minute cadence) and their pass-rate — we surface both raw and smoothed (5-min EMA). 5) Request volume by model-version and per-customer prefix cache hit rate.

For the onboarding dashboard: we prepare a read-only Grafana dashboard and a short instructions text file for access. For the exemption: our standard temporary exemption policy is a documented request, a mitigation plan (extra retries/circuit-breakers/cache priming), and security sign-off — typical approval turnaround is 24–48 hours for an emergency exemption.

Marcus
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dashboard-invite-instructions.txt
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightside.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement questions + request for interim access

Anna —

Happy to confirm the security gating for read-only access. We will: 1) provision a least-privilege Grafana API key scoped to the Brightside org and specific dashboard UIDs; 2) restrict IP ranges to Brightside's SSO/office networks where possible; 3) require an MSA amendment acknowledging that the dashboard is read-only telemetry (no customer PII will be exposed).

On temporary exemptions: approvals require a two-step flow for hosted customers — (a) Sales/SE submits a remediation plan and risk assessment; (b) Security and Ops sign-off. For low-risk, operational migrations we can do an expedited review within 24 hours. For anything that raises data-exposure risk we escalate to Legal and Compliance which can take longer.

If Brightside prefers, we can create an annex that sets the exact measurement windows for the contract (explicitly: 30-day rolling for contractual availability and p95 latency; alerting uses 5-min aggregates with synthetic checks at 1-min cadence).

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightside.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups: 1) Please send the exact dashboard URL and the short instructions file so I can circulate to our SREs. 2) For the exemption, we expect the request to include a rollback trigger and communications plan; is that standard? 3) Can you confirm that synthetic-check results will be retained for 90 days for our independent QA?

If you can push the read-only grant and the two attachments today, procurement can close this week.

Best,
Anna
